facts: Rearranged for the overlap, $|A \cap B| = |A| + |B| - |A \cup B|$.
In a universal set $\xi$, the number outside both sets is $|(A \cup B)'| = |\xi| - |A \cup B|$.
The number in $A$ only is $|A \cap B'| = |A| - |A \cap B|$.
steps: State the inclusion–exclusion rule: $|A \cup B| = |A| + |B| - |A \cap B|$.
Substitute the known counts into the equation.
Solve for the required unknown quantity.

foundation.question_text:
Two sets $A$ and $B$ satisfy $|A| = 14$, $|B| = 19$, and $|A \cap B| = 6$.
Find $|A \cup B|$.

In a group of students, $|A| = 25$, $|B| = 18$, and $|A \cup B| = 33$.
Find $|A \cap B|$.

Two sets satisfy $|A \cup B| = 40$, $|A| = 26$, and $|A \cap B| = 8$.
Find $|B|$.

Sets $P$ and $Q$ are disjoint ($P \cap Q = \varnothing$).
If $|P| = 15$ and $|Q| = 23$, find $|P \cup Q|$.

In a survey, $30$ people are in set $A$ and $11$ are in both $A$ and $B$.
How many people are in $A$ but not in $B$ ($|A \cap B'|$)?

A cohort has $|\xi| = 50$ students.
If $|A| = 22$, $|B| = 24$, and $|A \cap B| = 9$, find the number of students who are in neither set, $|(A \cup B)'|$.

development.question_text:
In a club of $70$ members, $44$ play tennis and $38$ play squash.
If every member plays at least one of the two sports, how many members play both tennis and squash?

A survey of $85$ music students found that $52$ play piano, some play guitar, $18$ play both, and $11$ play neither.
How many students play guitar?

In a school year group of $110$ students, $62$ study Art, $48$ study Music, and $21$ study both.
How many students study neither Art nor Music?

A class of $36$ students has $20$ students who study German and $17$ who study French.
If $5$ students study neither language, how many study German only?

A car dealership has $90$ vehicles in stock.
$55$ have leather seats, $46$ have a sunroof, and $15$ have neither feature.
How many vehicles have both leather seats and a sunroof?

In an office of $65$ workers, $39$ drink coffee, $28$ drink tea, and $12$ drink both.
How many workers drink exactly one of these beverages?
development.solution_text:
Coffee only:
$39 - 12 = 27$
Tea only:
$28 - 12 = 16$
Exactly one beverage:
$27 + 16$
$= 43$

development.question_text:
A commuter surveyed $120$ passengers on a train.
$58$ had a digital ticket, $47$ had a paper ticket, and $15$ had no ticket.
No passenger held both digital and paper tickets.
Verify this with the inclusion–exclusion rule and state the union size.

mastery.question_text:
In a competition with $100$ entrants, everyone submitted at least one entry in Category $A$ or Category $B$.
The number of entrants in Category $A$ only is three times the number in Category $B$ only.
If $20$ entrants submitted entries in both categories, find $|A|$.
mastery.solution_text:
Let $x$ be the number in Category $B$ only.
$3x + x + 20 = 100$
$4x + 20 = 100$
$4x = 80$
$x = 20$
Category $A$ only has $3(20) = 60$.
$|A| = 60 + 20$
$= 80$

mastery.question_text:
Two sets satisfy $|A| = 3x + 4$, $|B| = 2x + 9$, $|A \cap B| = x + 1$, and $|A \cup B| = 48$.
Find the value of $x$ and the size of set $A$.

In a group of $50$ people, $35$ speak English and $25$ speak Spanish.
What are the minimum and maximum possible values for the number of people who speak both languages, $|E \cap S|$?
mastery.solution_text:
Maximum intersection occurs when Spanish speakers are a subset of English speakers:
$\max(|E \cap S|) = 25$
Minimum intersection occurs when everyone in the group of $50$ speaks at least one language:
$\min(|E \cap S|) = 35 + 25 - 50$
$= 10$
Minimum is $10$, maximum is $25$.
